title: A Cipher for the Debt
premise: Tamsin Brightwater, a crash investigator haunted by the loss of his family in a disaster officially ruled an accident, has spent years living under an assumed name with a go-bag always packed. When Flight 611's records vanish mid-flight and the plane lands with no trace it ever existed, Tamsin recognizes the signature of a data-scrubbing operation he once helped design—and realizes someone is staging a catastrophic attack to be erased before it happens. Racing a countdown he can barely see, he allies with a disgraced air traffic controller and a teenage hacker who becomes the family he thought he'd lost, uncovering a conspiracy inside the very agency that once protected him. In the end, Tamsin must choose between staying invisible and going public with the truth that cost him everything, sacrificing his anonymity to ground the attack and finally claim a new kind of belonging.
about_author: Tamsin Dunmore is a former aviation safety analyst who left the industry after a decade of investigating accidents no one wanted explained. She writes thrillers from a coastal cottage in Cornwall, where she keeps her own go-bag out of habit.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Tamsin Brightwater's POV. On the anniversary of the crash that killed his family, Tamsin runs his morning ritual: check the exits, count the rows, touch the go-bag by the door. A colleague notices his polished lie of a life. Emotional beat: grief worn as routine, the reader learns what invisibility costs him daily.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A routine assignment reviewing near-miss reports puts Tamsin near the operations floor when an anomaly flickers: Flight 611's filing data corrupts, then deletes itself while the aircraft is airborne. His supervisor dismisses it as a glitch. Emotional beat: the first crack in Tamsin's carefully maintained numbness—his instincts wake up.

chapters.title: Six Eleven
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Mara Voss, a suspended air traffic controller drinking away her career, watched 611 on her scope and saw its transponder stutter. She files a report nobody wants. Emotional beat: two damaged professionals circling the same wound without knowing it, both dismissed by institutions they served.

chapters.title: Landing Without a Shadow
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Flight 611 lands at Heathrow—but manifests show no such flight ever departed, crew rosters are blank, and passengers' digital footprints have been scrubbed. Tamsin pulls a archived radar frame proving otherwise. Emotional beat: dread crystallizes into purpose; the lie of his own identity suddenly feels like practice for this moment.

chapters.title: The Scrubbing Signature
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Recognizing the deletion pattern as a tool he helped prototype years ago, Tamsin realizes whoever is doing this knows the system from the inside—and may know who he used to be. He packs the go-bag for real. Emotional beat: paranoia ignites; invisibility was never an option, only a delay.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Reads Ghosts
chapters.summary: New POV: Priya Okafor, seventeen, a hacker who archives deleted flight data as a hobby, contacts Tamsin after finding his old research buried in a scrubbed database. She has fragments of 611's true manifest. Emotional beat: wary connection—the first spark of found family, offered by a stranger who trusts too easily.

chapters.title: What the Manifest Says
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Priya reconstruct the passenger list and find one name flagged with a government seal: a defense contractor traveling with an unregistered cargo declaration. The 'accident' being planned isn't a crash—it's a cover story for something aboard. Emotional beat: the mystery sharpens into stakes; survival now means stopping, not escaping.

chapters.title: Voss's Radar Ghosts
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Tamsin tracks down Mara, whose suspension stemmed from reporting phantom radar returns months ago—the same corridor 611 flew. Together they map a pattern of test deletions leading toward a date eleven days out. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two people who trusted institutions learn to trust each other instead.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The trio decodes the pattern: a scheduled attack designed to look like mechanical failure, with every record pre-deleted so investigators will chase ghosts. Tamsin drafts an anonymous warning and hesitates—invisibility versus duty. Emotional beat: the central choice made flesh; he almost sends it unsigned, then signs nothing at all.

chapters.title: Someone Knows My Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. An old colleague from his former life appears at his door, friendly and wrong, asking questions about 611. Tamsin lies well but leaves shaken, certain he's been identified. He moves Priya to a safehouse. Emotional beat: terror of exposure; the past he buried is digging itself up.

chapters.title: The Agency That Raised Me
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter, Tamsin's POV. Tamsin reveals to Mara and Priya his true history: he built the deletion tools for the Aviation Integrity Unit after his family's crash was whitewashed using them. Emotional beat: confession as catharsis; the found family absorbs the truth of who he really is.

chapters.title: Cargo Bay Four
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya breaches a logistics network and finds the cargo: not a bomb but a biological containment unit scheduled for 'controlled release' over a populated corridor, framed as an accident to trigger emergency legislation worth billions. Emotional beat: horror escalates from personal to public; the price of survival is everyone's.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Their anonymous warning triggers a counter-move: Mara is arrested on fabricated charges, and Tamsin's safehouse address leaks. They scatter. Emotional beat: the conspiracy closes its fist; trust is tested when the plan costs one of them her freedom.

chapters.title: Trading Places
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. To free Mara, Tamsin offers the one thing he has: himself. He contacts his former handler and offers to return quietly if Mara walks. Emotional beat: sacrifice as belonging—he stops running and starts standing still for other people.

chapters.title: The Handler's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Face to face with Director Ellery Hask, Tamsin learns the attack is Hask's insurance policy against reform, and that Tamsin's family crash was the prototype run. The bargain: silence for safety. Emotional beat: rage and revelation braided together; the original wound was never an accident either.

chapters.title: Priya's Countermove
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Believing Tamsin has been captured or turned, Priya works alone, seeding the undeleted 611 data across forty mirrors worldwide—a dead-man's switch set to publish unless she resets it hourly. Emotional beat: the youngest member becomes the spine; found family fights even when it can't see its own.

chapters.title: Nine Hours
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Inside the agency under watch, Tamsin plays compliant while counting down to the attack window. He discovers the target corridor passes directly over the memorial where he visits row twelve's names. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the enemy has chosen his grief as camouflage.

chapters.title: Grounding 611
chapters.summary: Climax begins, alternating POV. Using Hask's own access codes, Tamsin files a genuine maintenance emergency on the attack aircraft while Mara, released in a prisoner transfer gone wrong, reaches an ATC friend to hold the corridor. Priya's mirrors begin publishing. Emotional beat: three separate gambits converging, each risking everything.

chapters.title: The Sky Remembers
chapters.summary: Climax, Tamsin's POV. The aircraft is forced down; the containment unit is seized on the tarmac; Hask orders Tamsin eliminated, but the publishing archive makes killing him pointless—exposure is already airborne. Hask is taken into custody by his own oversight board. Emotional beat: catharsis through action; the sky refuses to forget.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Public inquiry opens. Tamsin testifies under his real name, surrendering the alias forever, describing how records were made to vanish and how his family's crash was the rehearsal. Emotional beat: grief spoken aloud at last; invisibility traded for accountability.

chapters.title: A New Kind of Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Weeks later, Tamsin unpacks the go-bag permanently—or tries to. He keeps it half-packed, honest about what he is now: a man who stays. Priya calls it home; Mara brings case files for their new independent investigation unit. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; survival redefined as staying.

chapters.title: Flight Path Forward
chapters.summary: Epilogue, rotating short POVs. Priya ships her archiving tool to watchdog groups worldwide; Mara's name is cleared and reinstated; Tamsin stands at the memorial and reads row twelve aloud without flinching. A final image: a new flight departs cleanly, fully recorded, fully remembered. Emotional beat: quiet hope; the dead are honored by a world harder to erase.
